title: First-Year SIP Investor 12-Month Journey & Drop-Off Risk Matrix

stages.user_mental_state: High optimism, empowered, entering the world of investing.
stages.key_actions: KYC completion, bank mandate authorization (e-NACH), fund selection.
stages.dominant_friction: Mandate authentication failure, UPI auto-pay limits, confusion between Coin SIP and AMC SIP.
stages.grounded_insight: Starting an SIP is smooth and gamified; users feel a sense of accomplishment without anticipating subsequent market volatility.

stages.user_mental_state: Curious, vigilant, expecting immediate linear gains.
stages.key_actions: Frequent app logins (2–5x/week), checking 1-day P&L, comparing with bank balance.
stages.dominant_friction: Underwhelming returns shock (portfolio is +0.4% or -1.2%), T+2 Demat unit allocation delay, comparison to 7% risk-free FDs.
stages.grounded_insight: The gap between compounding dreams (15% CAGR) and initial nominal reality (₹15 gain on ₹1,000) causes immediate cognitive dissonance.

stages.user_mental_state: Apathy, checking fatigue, doubts about fund choice.
stages.key_actions: Reduced login frequency, ignoring monthly statements, seeking reassurance on Reddit or YouTube.
stages.dominant_friction: Market drawdown or sideways drift, lack of positive feedback from the app, isolation when seeing red returns.
stages.grounded_insight: With no emotional anchoring or milestone celebration, the monthly SIP debit begins to feel like a recurring bill rather than an asset purchase.

stages.key_actions: Balancing festive/vacation expenses, EMIs, or tax payments with discretionary savings.
stages.dominant_friction: Salary delay causing auto-debit bounce penalty (₹295+), difficulty pausing without complete cancellation.
stages.grounded_insight: When money is tight, the investment that feels unrewarding and flat is the very first expense to be paused or cancelled.

stages.stage_name: The Silent Lapse vs The Compounding Habit
stages.user_mental_state: Either entrenched habit or permanent abandonment.
stages.key_actions: Reviewing 1-year annual statement; either continuing automatically or letting paused SIP lapse permanently.
stages.dominant_friction: Three consecutive failed debits causing silent BSE StAR cancellation with zero re-engagement from the platform.
stages.grounded_insight: Over 70% of paused SIPs never resume unless proactive, low-friction re-activation paths exist.
